game.title: Panzergruppe Guderian: The Battle of Smolensk, July 1941
game.source: pdftotext extraction of PGG rules counters map v1.pdf (coordinator scratchpad, page-01..08.txt); crt.txt (typed CRT/TEC/supply summary); amendments.txt (Panzergruppe Guderian II fan variant, Tim Alanthwaite 2012); errata.txt (Clarifications, Errata and Addenda)

sides.side: Panzergruppe Guderian. Has no combat units on the map at the start of the game; enters entirely by reinforcement (2.0).
The Red Army defending the Dnepr and Smolensk.
sides.note: The two sides are asymmetric in mechanism, not just order of battle: only the Soviet has Rail Movement, Leaders and Untried units; only the German has a second (Mechanized) Movement Phase.

map.hex-ids: Two-digit column then two-digit row, no letter component (unlike The Russian Campaign's row-letter scheme). Grid is flat-topped, offset odd; the sheet's id-format is "{col:02}{row:02}", col-start 1, row-start 1. Smolensk is 2117; the German west-edge supply road hex is 0120.
map.hex-terrain: Infantry (not motorized) pays 1 MP; all other unit types pay 2 MP. No stop is required by the text supplied.
Supply may be traced into a Swamp hex but not through one.
May not be entered or crossed by movement; no combat may be resolved across a Lake hexside (see the lake-hexside hexside-terrain); supply may not be traced through.

A defender doubled and a Victory Point objective (15.1): Vitebsk 0513, Orsha 0420, Mogilev 0424, Smolensk 2117, Roslavl 2625, Yelnya, Rzhev 3901, Gzhatsk 4606, Vyazma 3915, Kaluga 5619, plus VP hexes 5907 and 5915 with no city glyph.
No combat effect. Drawn on the sheet as the "town" glyph: Velizh 1509, Bely 3005, Mstislavl 1524, Krichev 1427.
map.hexside-terrain: Germans pay 2 extra MP to cross, Soviets 1. Doubles the defender only if every attacking unit attacks across a River hexside (9.32); roads are considered to cross rivers for German supply tracing even though normal movement may not use a road to cross one (11.13, corrected by errata from the rulebook's misprinted cross-reference "11.14").

May not be crossed by movement; no combat may be resolved across it; supply may not be traced through it. Stronger than a plain movement block: attacks across a lake hexside are not merely undoubled, they are disallowed outright.

Movement along a road pays this cost instead of the hex's terrain cost: half a Movement Point for a mechanized/motorized/armour/cavalry unit, one full Movement Point for other infantry (not motorized). Also a network; see below. German Supply must trace along Road hexes to hex 0120 on the west edge (11.1).
map.network: Drawn centre to centre (6.7, 11.1). Carries the Road movement discount and is the German Supply network: a German unit must reach hex 0120 by an unbroken chain of Road hexes.

Soviet-only Rail Movement network, drawn centre to centre (6.3). Affects neither supply nor normal movement (6.35) -- its only function is the Rail Movement mode. Mutable: a German unit moving through a Soviet rail hex may cut the line (errata 6.37); Soviet units may not rail-move into or through a cut hex; repair happens only by a Soviet combat unit entering the cut hex during ordinary movement, and Rail Movement over the repaired line resumes the following turn.
map.space: Eliminated Untried Soviet units, still face-down; drawn from once the counter pool proper is exhausted (12.4). The absolute ceiling on units in play is the number of physical counters, regardless of source.
Soviet divisions not yet in play, from which set-up and reinforcement divisions are drawn at random by type, face down (12.1).
Scheduled Soviet Leaders waiting to enter, each with the turns left before it may (16.1).
German counters waiting to enter, each with the turns left before it may (16.2).
map.note: Other hex-centred data: the six numbered Soviet Provisional Reinforcement entrance areas (14.1); the lettered Soviet entrance points V, W, X, Z (16.1); the lettered German entrance areas A-H (16.2); the Soviet initial-deployment hexes/areas (5.1). These are authored, scenario-specific placements, not a general region layer.

The westernmost two hexrows (all hexes with column "01" or "02") are a rules-significant region named directly by column rather than by a sheet layer: forbidden to voluntary or involuntary Soviet entry through turn 6 (6.4), and mandatory for the 13th and 20th Armies to clear entirely on turn 1 (5.23).

counters.unit-type: Placed Untried (12.0); true Attack-Defense-Movement is revealed only at the instant of first combat or Overrun (12.2). One step: any loss eliminates it (9.62).
Placed Untried, as soviet-rifle (12.0). Counted as armoured for set-up and reinforcement purposes (amendments 3.4); more are printed than are needed for play.
Four steps: 9-7, 4-7, 2-7, 1-7 (9.63). Does not qualify for Divisional Integration (7.3).

Two steps, the second printed on the counter's reverse (9.63). One Panzer and two Panzer Grenadier regiments; qualifies for Divisional Integration when the whole division is stacked together with no foreign unit present (7.3).

Two regiments, except Das Reich, which has three (7.3). Independent regiments GD (Grossdeutschland) and Lehr may stack with a two-regiment motorized division without breaking its integration (amendments 7.3).
Two steps (9.63). Does not qualify for Divisional Integration; the Soviet Player receives no Victory Points for its elimination (15.12).

An army-level command organisation, not merely a figurehead (10.0): its one printed rating is simultaneously the Line-of-Communications Radius, the maximum Combat Points it may add to a directly-stacked attack, and its own Defense Strength (10.1). Has no Attack Strength (10.22); may not Overrun by itself (6.53).
Placed on a unit Disrupted by a failed or partial Overrun defense (6.6); removed automatically in the owner's next Disruption Removal Phase.
No ZOC, no combat capability, does not count against stacking (13.1). Three provided.
No ZOC (13.4). Usable on at most three turns in the game, never the last.
Placed on a Soviet Railroad hex a German unit has moved through (errata 6.37); six provided. Blocks Soviet Rail Movement into or through the hex.

list.name: Fields printed on a unit counter
list.item: Regiment ids embed the parent division, e.g. 20/12 for the 20th Panzer Regiment of the 12th Panzer Division (2.0).
German: Attack-Defense, or a single Combat Strength; Soviet: Attack-Defense-Movement when revealed, a question mark when Untried.

phase.name: Game Turn
phase.step: Every reinforcement still waiting comes a turn nearer.
A move follows one connected path its units can afford, through no enemy unit, stopping in the first enemy zone of control.
An attacker is no Leader, is not Disrupted and attacks once; a Soviet attacker is within a working Leader's radius; a defender is attacked once a phase.
The path's movement points are spent, and rail movement counts against the eight units of the turn.
Rail hexes German units passed are noted, a Soviet unit's march repairs a cut, and the hex a unit left to enter an enemy zone is kept.
A Victory Point hex belongs to the last side to occupy it or pass through it.
After Game-Turn Twelve the Soviet total is taken from the German and the level of victory is read.

phase.name: Initial Set-Up
phase.note: The Soviet units stand as the scenario places them; the German Player places his three Air Interdiction Markers before the first Soviet turn (13.2).

phase.name: Soviet Player-Turn
phase.step: Cities the German Player held at the end of his last player-turn and the Soviet Player now occupies score their recapture.
Units that entered this player-turn lose their free supply; the turn's rail and South-Western Front counts start again.

phase.name: Movement Phase
phase.step: Supply for movement, and each unit's Leader radius for overruns, are judged as the phase begins.
A die for the 16th and one for the 19th Army: on 4 to 6 the army stands for the turn.
The turn's scheduled divisions are owed at their entrance hexes.
One Provisional Reinforcement is rolled for and placed.
The first-turn armies move as 5.2 requires.
The German Air Interdiction Markers come off.
Overstacked units are eliminated.
The phase's movement points, halts and passages are forgotten.
phase.note: Check Supply; move any or all units; conduct Overruns; bring in Reinforcements. German Air Interdiction Markers are removed at the end of this Phase.

phase.name: Combat Phase
phase.step: Overstacked units are eliminated.
Units retreated onto friendly stacks count as defenders again.
phase.note: Soviet units may attack adjacent German units.

phase.name: Disruption Removal Phase
phase.step: Disruption comes off the Soviet units.

phase.name: Soviet Interdiction Phase
phase.note: At most three times in the game, never turn 12: place a Soviet Interdiction Marker.

phase.name: German Player-Turn
phase.step: The cities the German Player holds with a line to the west edge are recorded.
The Soviet Interdiction Marker comes off.
Units that entered this player-turn lose their free supply.

phase.name: Initial Movement Phase
phase.step: Supply for movement is judged as the phase begins.
Overstacked units are eliminated.
The phase's movement points, halts and passages are forgotten.
phase.note: Check Supply; bring in Reinforcements; move units; conduct Overruns.

phase.name: Combat Phase
phase.step: Overstacked units are eliminated.
Units retreated onto friendly stacks count as defenders again.
phase.note: German units may attack adjacent Soviet units, with the Divisional Integration bonus where it applies.

phase.name: Mechanized Movement Phase
phase.step: Supply for movement is judged again as the phase begins.
Overstacked units are eliminated.
The phase's movement points, halts and passages are forgotten.
phase.note: Only Panzer, Mech, Motorized and Cavalry units (german-panzer, german-motorized, german-cavalry) may move, and may conduct further Overruns. Infantry may not act in this Phase.

phase.name: Disruption Removal Phase
phase.step: Disruption comes off the German units.

phase.name: Air Interdiction Phase
phase.note: Place German Air Interdiction Markers for the following Soviet turn; remove any Soviet Interdiction Marker.

sequence.rule: The 16th Army (hex 2216) and the 19th Army (hex 1414) may move on turn 1 only if a die roll of 1, 2 or 3 is made for that army; otherwise it stands in place, shuffling at most one hex per unit if needed to satisfy stacking.

The 13th and 20th Armies must expend their full Movement Allowance, may not end the phase in hex-columns 01 or 02, may not re-enter a hex, may move only north, south or east, and may not use Rail Movement.

stacking.enforced: end of the Friendly Movement Phase and throughout the Combat Phase
stacking.rule: The Soviet Player may stack up to four units in a hex, rather than three, if at least one of the four is a Leader.

If every regiment of a German Panzer or Motorized Infantry Division is stacked together, with no unit from any other division present, the stack's Combat Strength is doubled for both attack and defense. German Infantry and Cavalry Divisions never qualify. Losing any regiment of the division disqualifies it from the bonus. The independent regiments GD and Lehr may stack with a two-regiment motorized division without breaking its integration (amendments 7.3).

zoc.name: Zone of control
zoc.note: Own hex plus the six adjacent hexes. Extends across River hexsides; does not extend across Lake hexsides (8.17). No stacking of effect from multiple ZOCs on one hex (8.18). Friendly units, but not Friendly ZOC, negate an enemy ZOC for supply and leadership-radius tracing and for retreat, never for movement (8.15).
zoc.rule: Disrupted units project no Zone of Control.
If a unit is in an enemy-controlled hex, the enemy unit is equally in that unit's Zone of Control; the two are jointly affected.
A unit must stop the instant it enters an enemy-controlled hex and may not leave voluntarily; it may leave only as a result of combat, or by Overrun (6.5).

movement.mode: Pay the entry cost of each hex from the Terrain Effects Chart, or the Road hexside cost when moving along a road. Movement Points may not be saved, banked, or transferred between units or phases (6.12, 6.23). German mechanized units get a fresh allowance in the Mechanized Movement Phase.

Up to eight combat units (each Soviet armour/mechanized division counting as three) plus any number of Leaders, thirty hexes, hex to adjacent connected Rail hex only, starting and finishing on a Railroad hex, never through an enemy ZOC. Terrain has no cost effect; German Air Interdiction raises the per-hex cost (13.31). No Supply or Leader-radius requirement to use the bonus (6.34).

Move the participating units, all from one hex, adjacent to the target; pay three extra Movement Points; resolve combat immediately on the ordinary Combat Results Table at halved Attack Strength (see the overrun-halving modifier). If the target hex is vacated, move into it at no further cost and continue moving, and Overrunning again, with any remaining points, unless now in an enemy ZOC. A split or Engaged result, or any attacker loss or retreat, halts the Overrunning unit(s) for the rest of the Phase (6.52). Not Advance After Combat: the free entry into a vacated hex is movement, not an advance (6.57, 9.88).
movement.rule: A Soviet unit that begins the Movement Phase outside its coordinating Leader's Radius may not conduct an Overrun.
Movement Allowance ten; moves like a Motorized unit on roads but like Infantry in Forest; may use Rail Movement alone and does not count against the eight-unit Rail cap.

No Soviet unit may voluntarily or involuntarily enter hex-columns 01 or 02. A unit forced to retreat there is eliminated instead. Soviet units may still trace Supply and Leadership Radius through those hexrows.
A unit not in Supply has its Movement Allowance halved, fractions dropped, never below one.

trace.name: German supply, via the road network
trace.sources: hex 0120 on the west map edge
trace.checked: start of each Movement Phase for movement; instant of combat or Overrun for combat
trace.segment: Twenty hexes from the unit to reach some Road hex, uninterrupted by enemy units, enemy-controlled hexes or impassable terrain.
That Road hex to hex 0120, along an unbroken chain of Road hexes, likewise uninterrupted.

trace.name: German supply, direct movement-point trace
trace.sources: any hex on the west map edge
trace.checked: start of each Movement Phase for movement; instant of combat or Overrun for combat
trace.segment: Twenty Movement Points, not hexes, counted by the tracing unit's own type, directly to any west-edge hex. The river-crossing cost is paid regardless of whether a road is present (errata 11.13); terrain otherwise applies as for normal movement.

trace.name: Soviet supply, relayed through a Leader
trace.sources: the east map edge, reached by relaying through a Soviet Leader
trace.checked: start of each Movement Phase for movement; instant of combat or Overrun for combat
trace.segment: Line of Communications: the combat unit to any Soviet Leader, no more hexes than that Leader's own printed Radius rating (a per-Leader value, not a game-wide constant). May not pass through enemy units, enemy ZOCs, or impassable terrain; into but not through a Swamp hex (amendments 10.31).
Line of Supply: that Leader to the east map edge, any length, under the same blocking rules. The Leader itself needs no line to another Leader (11.24).

supply.rule: Units may remain out of Supply indefinitely; they are never eliminated for lack of Supply alone.
All units are considered in Supply during the first Player-Turn of their entrance into the game.
Railroads carry neither supply nor normal movement; they affect nothing but Rail Movement, so a Rail Cut marker has no supply effect by itself.

resolver.name: Combat Results Table
resolver.note: An enemy-occupied hex may be attacked by every unit that can bear from the six adjacent hexes; all units in the target hex are attacked as a single Defense Strength; no unit may attack, or be attacked, more than once per Combat Phase. Attacks worse than 1-3 or better than 10-1 are treated as the nearest end column.

list.name: Combat results
list.item: All attacking units eliminated. Opposing Player may advance one or two hexes, the first the vacated hex.
All defending units eliminated. Opposing Player may advance one or two hexes, the first the vacated hex.
The attacker loses one step from any one unit, or retreats the whole attacking stack one hex; not both (9.65).
As A1, but two steps or two hexes.
The defender loses one step from any one unit, or retreats the whole defending stack one hex; not both.
As D1, but two steps or two hexes.
Engaged: each side loses one step and remains in place. No retreat option; neither side may advance.

resolver.rule: In a split result (e.g. D1*/A1) the defender's result is applied first, then the attacker's. Only the attacker may then advance, and only if the defending hex was vacated; the defender never advances in a split result.

A defender result earned during an Overrun (marked "*" above) also Disrupts the surviving defending unit(s): loss of Zone of Control, cannot move or attack, defends normally, and a Disrupted Leader cannot function as a Leader (6.62, 6.64).

combat.modifier: Applied before terrain multipliers and before halving for Overrun or being out of Supply (amendments 9.35, 11.37).
Major City and River (if every attacker crosses a River hexside) each double; Forest doubles. Effects are cumulative additively, minus one: Forest plus River gives x3, not x4 (9.33).
Combat Strength halved, fractions dropped, never below one. Applied after Divisional Integration doubling, before Overrun halving.
Halving is the final adjustment; fractions are dropped after it. Worked example: a Panzer Division (8) doubled for integration (16), halved for out-of-supply (8), halved again for Overrun (4).

A Soviet Leader stacked directly with an attacking unit may add its Leadership Value to that unit's attack, never more than the unit's own post-modifier Strength; the addition may not be split across units.
combat.rule: A Soviet unit revealed as 0-0-6 is removed from play at the instant of revelation. Two specific 0-1-6 Rifle Divisions remain in play but may only ever defend; if committed to an attack before revelation, they must retreat as a Leader does under Case 10.23.

A Soviet combat unit may not attack unless it is within a Soviet Leader's Radius; it may attack at half Strength while out of Supply if still within radius, and may defend at half Strength without any Leader present.

retreat.note: Retreat is always optional in place of a step loss (9.71, 9.65). Routed by the opposing Player, even for split results (9.72). May not pass through an enemy unit or enemy ZOC unless the hex holds a Friendly unit; prefers a vacant hex; a retreat that would violate stacking eliminates the excess unit instead (9.73). A unit retreated onto a Friendly-occupied hex adds nothing to its defense and is eliminated automatically if that hex later suffers any combat result (9.75).
retreat.rule: Victorious units may advance into the vacated hex or along the Path of Retreat, ignoring enemy ZOCs, stopping where they choose, immediately and before other combat is resolved; they may not then attack or be attacked that Phase. If the whole defending stack was eliminated, the advance may be up to two hexes, the first of which must be the vacated hex.
Advance After Combat never applies to Overrun; its free entry into a vacated hex is ordinary movement.
A Soviet unit forced to retreat into hex-column 01 or 02 is eliminated instead.

game.randomizer: One six-sided die for combat, the first-turn Soviet movement check (5.21), and the Provisional Reinforcement entrance roll (14.11).

victory.condition: Total each side's Victory Points; subtract the Soviet total from the German total; read the Level of Victory from the schedule below.

list.name: German Victory Points for occupation
list.item: Smolensk: 25 (reduced by two per Game Turn from Turn 5 onward, amendments 15.11)
Yelnya: 10 (hex from the original 1976 map; the sheet XML, traced from the Cyrillic map, does not mark it)

victory.rule: Occupation means a German combat unit in every hex of the city, or the last Player to have passed a unit through them, with a line of hexes free of Enemy units or Enemy ZOCs (negated by Friendly units) traced from the city to the west map edge.

One Victory Point per South-Western Front division the Soviet Player uses among the first five, two for each of the next five; fifteen if all ten are used (the rulebook's cross-reference "13.23" is corrected by errata to "14.23").
One Victory Point for each entire German division eliminated, except the Cavalry Division, for which none is awarded; no points for individual regiments alone.

Two Victory Points each time the Soviet Player recaptures a city that the German Player held, with the west-edge line described in german-vp-occupation, at the end of the previous German Player-Turn. May be earned repeatedly for the same city.

Errata addition: the historical outcome was a German Marginal Victory. Players who want that reading may treat a German Marginal Victory as a draw and require a German Strategic Victory or better for a German win.

game.rule: All Soviet combat units, set-up or reinforcement, are placed face-down (Untried), chosen by type from the counter pool without either Player knowing the true Strength.

A unit is revealed only at the instant it is committed to combat or Overrun, not at the start of the Combat Phase; once committed it may not be withdrawn or reallocated even at unfavourable odds. A preceding combat earlier in the same phase can change what a later attack sees.
While Untried, even a unit that will reveal as zero-strength still projects a Zone of Control and blocks supply and retreat lines.

Eliminated Untried units go to the dead pile, still face-down, and may be drawn as further reinforcements once the counter pool proper is exhausted. The counter-count ceiling on units in play is absolute regardless of source.

No farther east than hex-row 40 (inclusive), unless the German Player holds both Smolensk hexes and has traced a Line of Communications to the west edge, one turn after taking the city; recapture by the Soviet Player reverts the restriction. Placed once before the game for the first Soviet turn, then each Air Interdiction Phase.

On a Railroad hex, adds four points to Rail Movement cost through it. On any other hex, adds one Movement Point for Soviet units entering it. At most one marker per hex; all removed at the end of the following Soviet Movement Phase; no effect on Soviet supply tracing.

Placed anywhere at the end of the Soviet Player-Turn, uncounted against stacking, not on a German-occupied hex; has the same Movement Point effect on German units as the German marker has on Soviet units, for both German Movement Phases, and additionally interrupts German supply tracing through its hex. Removed at the end of the German Player-Turn.

Each turn, one die roll selects one of six numbered entrance hexes/areas; one Untried Rifle Division arrives there, in addition to the scheduled reinforcements (16.1). If the rolled area is fully German-occupied or German-controlled, the unit enters instead at the nearest open hex toward the east edge. May not be saved or accumulated.

Up to five Rifle Divisions per turn, ten for the whole game, entering any southern-edge Railroad hex at or east of entrance hex Z; entirely voluntary; costs German Victory Points (see german-vp-swf); no Leader accompanies them.
The Soviet Player does not receive scheduled reinforcements on Game-Turn Twelve; the rulebook's Section 16.1 list is authoritative over the map's printed reinforcement table.
On Game-Turn Two, Entrance Area B, the German Player receives the 26th Infantry Division, not the 16th as the rulebook misprints.
On Game-Turn Seven, Entrance Area E, the German Player also receives the 268th Infantry Division.
game.note: Rail Cut (errata addition to the AH reprint, 6.37)
game.rule: A German combat unit moving through a Soviet Railroad hex may cut that line; mark it with a Rail Cut marker (six provided). Soviet units may not use Rail Movement into or through a cut hex.

A Soviet combat unit entering the cut hex during ordinary (non-rail) movement removes the marker; Rail Movement over the repaired line resumes the turn following the repair. The German Player may instead move a unit back over his own cut to free the marker for a new cut elsewhere.
game.note: Divisional Integration and Overrun order of operations (amendments 9.35, 11.37)
game.rule: A division's Combat Strength is doubled for Divisional Integration before it is multiplied for terrain effects, and before it is halved for conducting an Overrun or being out of Supply.
game.note: Optional systems from the amendments, not enabled by default
game.rule: Before play, both Players secretly bid a Victory Point adjustment to play the German side; the higher (or least negative) bid wins the German side and suffers that adjustment against the final total.

Replaces the flat per-division Soviet award with: one-half Victory Point per German step lost to a German attack, one point per German step lost to a Soviet attack, plus 3/2/1 additional points for eliminating an entire Panzer/Panzergrenadier/Infantry-or-Cavalry division (net per-division totals: Panzer 6, Panzergrenadier 4, Infantry 3, Cavalry 2).
Divisional Integration doubling, terrain multiplication, and Overrun/out-of-supply halving do not commute; apply them in that order (see integration-order).
An Untried reveal happens at the instant of its own combat, not at the start of the Combat Phase, so an earlier combat in the same phase can change what a later attack in that phase sees.
German Air Interdiction Markers are removed at the end of the Soviet Movement Phase, not the end of the whole Soviet Player-Turn, even though they were placed the German turn before.
Rail Cut repair takes effect the turn after the repairing movement, not immediately.
